name: The PM²-Agile Model
one_liner: Agile and Lean practice tailored onto PM² governance; it replaces nothing.
purpose: PM²-Agile is not a new Agile philosophy or approach: it tailors proven Agile and Lean practices and connects them to PM², so teams can apply Agile values while keeping enterprise awareness and compliance at the overall project level. It is framed by the PM² methodology, which supplies the governance model and the artefacts throughout the whole lifecycle. What changes is how the delivery work is organised, not whether the project is governed.
meta: A tailoring of Agile & Lean onto PM², not a replacement for it
How delivery work is run; governance, phases and artefacts stay
Seven — roles, lifecycle integration, themes, ceremonies, artefacts, glossary, tools
12 PM²-Agile principles, adapted from the Agile Manifesto
Five — Iteration Planning, Daily Stand-up, Release Planning, Iteration Review, Iteration Retrospective
BM · PM · TeCo · PrOw · ArOw · ATeM

diagram.sec: A. What PM² supplies and PM²-Agile keeps
items: A project governance structure: directing, managing and performing layers
A serial four-phase lifecycle with clear project-approval milestones
Process guidelines, artefact templates and guidelines for using them
A set of effective mindsets (the 11 PM² Mindsets and the IAQs)
PM²-Agile does not replace any part of PM² — it expands it (p. 2)

diagram.sec: B. What PM²-Agile adds — the seven elements (p. 15)
items: 1. Roles & Responsibilities, as an extension to the PM² governance
2. Integration with the overall PM² project lifecycle
3. Core Themes
4. A key set of Ceremonies
5. A set of suggested Agile artefacts, extending the PM² artefacts
6. An Agile glossary
7. Agile Tools & Techniques

diagram.sec: C. Where the Agile team sits — the A-PCT
items: PM²-Agile expands the Performing layer only (p. 61)
There is one project team and only one Project Core Team (PCT)
A PCT applying PM²-Agile is called the Agile PCT (A-PCT)
Four core roles: Team Coordinator, Product Owner, Architecture Owner, Agile Team Member
Agile roles are not people; the roles are fulfilled by people

diagram.sec: D. The rhythm — three cycle levels, one CIR beat
items: Daily cycles → Iterations → Releases (Fig. 3.10, p. 19)
Every cycle follows the CIR rhythm: Coordinate, Implement, Review
Value is delivered and feedback collected at all three levels
Be serial in the large, and iterative in the small (driver, p. 23)

diagram.sec: E. The five ceremonies, mapped to CIR (p. 41)
items: Coordinate → Iteration Planning · Daily Stand-up · Release Planning
Implement → no prescribed ceremony; engineering and co-creation techniques instead
Review → Iteration Review · Iteration Retrospective
Ceremonies are not a silver bullet: they need roles, artefacts, tools and mindsets around them
Lean UX · Planning · Coordination and Reporting · Requirements
Estimation and Prioritisation · Risks · Quality · Evolution & Change
Architecture · Compliance & Security · Development
Software Configuration Management · Testing · Deployment & Transition

diagram.sec: G. Artefacts, in three groups (§3.5, p. 24; §7, p. 67)
items: IT governance: Business Case, Project Charter, Architecture Overview, Operational Model — mandatory when the solution includes an information system
Agile-specific: Development Handbook, Development Work Plan (Work Items List + Release Plan + Iteration Plan), Test Plans, Deployment Plan
Coordination & reporting: Development Status Report, PM²-Agile Logs (incl. the Retrospectives Log)
Agile does not mean no documentation, but just enough — defined by the project and by corporate needs for transparency, traceability and control
PM²-Agile is not one-size-fits-all; tailor it and let it evolve each iteration or release
Tailoring changes process steps, artefact contents or the distribution of responsibilities
The Development Handbook documents how and why PM²-Agile was tailored
Responsibilities for review and approval are recorded in a RASCI table

fields.what: An offering that enables Agile practices in any PM² project by tailoring proven Agile and Lean practice and connecting it to PM².
fields.who: CoEPM² owns it · the A-PCT applies it
fields.pollux: POLLUX is delivered PM²-Agile; its predecessor CASTOR was delivered PM² core.

fields.what: The governance layers, Business Case, Project Charter, phases and approval milestones all remain. Agile changes how the Executing work is delivered.
fields.pollux: Medici funds POLLUX because he still gets a Business Case, a Charter and gates.

fields.what: Chosen when requirements are genuinely uncertain and value arrives incrementally; PM² acknowledges uncertainty and endorses an enterprise-aware Agile approach.
fields.who: Argued in the Business Case · agreed with the AGB
fields.pollux: Nobody agrees what the exposure report should contain; each quarter the requirements change.

fields.what: Twelfth principle: Agile practice must respect IT governance, enterprise architecture and interoperability, and collaborate with teams following other approaches.
fields.pollux: National-authority access pulls DPC Brandeis and LISO Turing into the Work Items List.

fields.what: The Agile Manifesto principles adopted with modifications: early continuous delivery, welcome change, deliver value frequently, quality, simplicity, sustainable pace, enterprise awareness.
fields.pollux: A new report view in one iteration instead of one quarter is principle one in practice.

fields.what: Three shifts from the Manifesto: focus on solution delivery, on all project stakeholders, and on the organisational ecosystem and its improvement.
fields.pollux: Risk, the Board and Finance are all stakeholders; none of them is "the customer".

fields.what: "There is no such thing as an Agile project. There are only PM²-Agile projects." Agile team members are members of the PM² Project Core Team.
fields.pollux: Gantt is told POLLUX is agile and assumes no schedule; there are three levels of plan.

fields.what: The name for a Project Core Team applying PM²-Agile. There is one project team and only one PCT; PM²-Agile expands the performing layer.
fields.pollux: Lovelace, Curie, Einstein, plus Lamarr, Babbage and Eiffel building.

fields.what: Facilitator and team coach; creates and maintains the conditions for delivery, facilitates planning, estimation and decisions, reports progress to the PM.
fields.pollux: Ada Lovelace, the CASTOR business analyst, promoted to Team Coordinator.

fields.what: The single voice of the stakeholders inside the A-PCT; continuously prioritises the Work Items List and clarifies domain questions.
fields.pollux: Marie Curie, Head of Reporting; nobody argues with her acceptance criteria.

fields.what: Solution architect responsible for the team's architecture decisions; guides rather than dictates, and is expected to deliver work like any other member.
fields.pollux: Albert Einstein, seconded from Enterprise Architecture; every enabler story starts with him.

fields.what: Builds the information system: analysis, design, programming, testing, planning and estimation. Cross-disciplinary generalists rather than narrow specialists.
fields.who: Decides how the work is done
fields.pollux: Hedy Lamarr, Charles Babbage and Gustave Eiffel, seconded lead from Levallois Systems.

fields.what: Unchanged PM² role: delegate of the Project Owner on the daily life of the project, collaborating with the PM and supporting the PrOw on priorities.
fields.pollux: Grace Hopper, Senior Loan Operations Officer, still the business's daily voice.

fields.what: Responsible for the whole project and its deliverables; informed of iteration goals and outcomes, accountable for the development plans and reports.
fields.pollux: You keep the PM² role; PM²-Agile does not delete it.

fields.what: Coordinate, Implement, Review — the beat every cycle follows, whatever its duration: daily cycles, iterations and releases alike.
fields.pollux: Stand-up each morning, two-week iterations, roughly quarterly releases.

fields.what: Fourteen areas of knowledge where PM² concepts had to be adjusted for Agile values — from Lean UX and Planning through to Deployment & Transition.
fields.pollux: Compliance & Security is live: national-authority access, DPC and LISO reviews.

fields.what: Business Case, Project Charter, Architecture Overview and Operational Model — mandatory for projects whose solution includes an information system.
fields.who: PM accountable · ArOw responsible for the last two
fields.pollux: Business Case and Charter approved 12 Oct 2028, before any iteration existed.

fields.what: Records how and why PM²-Agile was tailored for this project: deviations, roles, tools, formats, review formality, and a RASCI for approvals.
fields.pollux: Baselined 27 Nov 2028 with the Development Work Plan, before the RfE gate.

fields.what: Container of three levels of plan: the Work Items List, the Release Plan and the Iteration Plans. Becomes part of the Project Work Plan.
fields.pollux: The answer to Gantt: agile POLLUX has a schedule, at three levels of detail.

fields.what: Responsible, Accountable, Supports, Consulted, Informed. Every PM²-Agile ceremony and artefact carries one, with columns BM, PM, TeCo, PrOw, ArOw, ATeM.
fields.pollux: Recorded in the POLLUX Development Handbook so nobody re-argues who decides.

traps: "An Agile project" is wrong wording — there are only PM²-Agile projects.
PM²-Agile is not Scrum; Scrum covers construction, not the whole project lifecycle.
Agile teams do document and do plan — just enough, at three levels.
Roles are not people: one person may hold two roles, and ArOw also builds.
Tailoring is recorded in the Development Handbook, not in the Project Charter.
